title: DNA evidence in the narrative economy of crime reporting
abstract: A close view of how the news media disseminates and circulates evidentiary breakthroughs in cold cases offers insights into the narrative economy of crime reporting. Forensic evidence, and especially DNA traces, are objects of public fascination. In high-profile crime coverage, news media translates complex forensic science issues into formats accessible to a broad readership. This article observes a progressive narrowing of interpretive space as technical details are simplified and narrativized, which skews public perceptions of crime and criminal justice in favour of misleading crime narratives. These processes limit the public’s interpretive avenues, leaving little room for accountability following miscarriages of justice.
